data.title: What ASML Doubters Overlooked
data.description:
If ASML sat on your watchlist instead of in your portfolio, the gain over the last year may feel like a missed shot. Holding ASML over the past year would have returned 40.9%, including dividends. That outcome raises a sharper question. Back on 20 November 2025, when analysts still argued over how fast EUV and High NA tools might spread, what signals could have helped you judge whether AI driven wafer starts would really justify those bullish adoption assumptions?

ASML has already moved. Pinpoint other ways to investigate the theme among 53 AI infrastructure stocks.

The Argument You Would Have Been Weighing On ASML

The shares cost €890 at the start of the period. At that point, ASML sat between two very different stories about how deep the AI driven wafer cycle might run and how much lithography spending governments and chipmakers would really commit to.

On the bullish side, one narrative saw a Fair Value of €950, a price implied by expectations that AI, cloud and data center demand would drive EUV and High NA tools, plus service contracts, far beyond prior cycles. That view leaned on an assumption that earnings could reach €13.9b by about 2028 with P/E at 31.6x.

The more cautious script pinned Fair Value at €769, a level based on assumed revenue growth of 7.2% and profit margin of 30.4% over roughly three years. It treated geopolitical risk and export controls as central threats, with tariffs and restrictions on China seen as potential brakes on ASML’s addressable market and High NA adoption.

What The Results Changed For The ASML Thesis

Record Q3 2026 figures gave the bullish ASML story its strongest support. Reported revenue reached €11.7b versus €7.5b a year earlier, and net income moved from €2.1b to €5.0b. Net margin shifted from 28.3% to 42.5%. Management also reported demand for AI related tools that supply cannot fully match. Rising export control risk around China still challenged the upside case, so the evidence cut both ways.

The whole debate turned on how much AI driven lithography demand would show up in actual orders and profitability. For any other chip equipment group, the same check is simple. Track multi quarter revenue, backlog comments and reported net margin against the story being told about AI and wafer starts.

What ASML’s Run Leaves You Paying For Today

ASML now trades at €1,168 after a 40.9% gain over the past year, and this Narrative’s Fair Value view sits below that level. The gap reflects concern that today’s quote already charges a premium for ASML’s position in advanced lithography.

According to Thomas_Regrettier, a Simply Wall St Community investor who wrote the Narrative, the crux for anyone buying at today’s price is whether ASML can keep its geopolitical exposure contained while remaining the dominant supplier of leading edge tools to a very small group of customers.

"ASML’s story is one of quiet dominance at the heart of global tech. Founded in the Netherlands in 1984, ASML started as a joint venture between Philips and ASM International. Over the decades, it evolved into the sole supplier in the world of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines, which are essential for manufacturing the most advanced semiconductor chips (like those powering AI, smartphones, and data centers)."

data.title: Is It Smart To Buy Xylem Inc. (NYSE:XYL) Before It Goes Ex-Dividend?
data.description:
Xylem Inc. (NYSE:XYL) stock is about to trade ex-dividend in three days. The ex-dividend date is usually set to be one business day before the record date, which is the cut-off date on which you must be present on the company's books as a shareholder in order to receive the dividend. The ex-dividend date is important because any transaction on a stock needs to have been settled before the record date in order to be eligible for a dividend. Therefore, if you purchase Xylem's shares on or after the 24th of November, you won't be eligible to receive the dividend, when it is paid on the 22nd of December.

The company's next dividend payment will be US$0.43 per share. Last year, in total, the company distributed US$1.72 to shareholders. Last year's total dividend payments show that Xylem has a trailing yield of 1.8% on the current share price of US$95.24. Dividends are a major contributor to investment returns for long term holders, but only if the dividend continues to be paid. So we need to check whether the dividend payments are covered, and if earnings are growing.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Dividends are typically paid out of company income, so if a company pays out more than it earned, its dividend is usually at a higher risk of being cut. That's why it's good to see Xylem paying out a modest 37% of its earnings. A useful secondary check can be to evaluate whether Xylem generated enough free cash flow to afford its dividend. Fortunately, it paid out only 44% of its free cash flow in the past year.

data.description:

A Closer Look At Flowers Foods' Earnings

Many investors haven't heard of the accrual ratio from cashflow, but it is actually a useful measure of how well a company's profit is backed up by free cash flow (FCF) during a given period. To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. That is not intended to imply we should worry about a positive accrual ratio, but it's worth noting where the accrual ratio is rather high. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

Flowers Foods has an accrual ratio of -0.11 for the year to October 2026. Therefore, its statutory earnings were quite a lot less than its free cashflow. Indeed, in the last twelve months it reported free cash flow of US$354m, well over the US$30.0m it reported in profit. Flowers Foods shareholders are no doubt pleased that free cash flow improved over the last twelve months. However, that's not all there is to consider. We can see that unusual items have impacted its statutory profit, and therefore the accrual ratio.

The Impact Of Unusual Items On Profit

Flowers Foods' profit was reduced by unusual items worth US$190m in the last twelve months, and this helped it produce high cash conversion, as reflected by its unusual items. This is what you'd expect to see where a company has a non-cash charge reducing paper profits. While deductions due to unusual items are disappointing in the first instance, there is a silver lining. We looked at thousands of listed companies and found that unusual items are very often one-off in nature. And, after all, that's exactly what the accounting terminology implies. Flowers Foods took a rather significant hit from unusual items in the year to October 2026. As a result, we can surmise that the unusual items made its statutory profit significantly weaker than it would otherwise be.

Our Take On Flowers Foods' Profit Performance

data.title: Earnings Update: Nufarm Limited (ASX:NUF) Just Reported And Analysts Are Trimming Their Forecasts
data.description:
It's shaping up to be a tough period for Nufarm Limited (ASX:NUF), which a week ago released some disappointing full-year results that could have a notable impact on how the market views the stock. It was a pretty negative result overall, with revenues of AU$3.2b missing analyst predictions by 2.3%. Additionally, the business reported a statutory loss of AU$0.26 per share, larger than the analysts had forecast prior to the result. Following the result, the analysts have updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. We've gathered the most recent statutory forecasts to see whether the analysts have changed their earnings models, following these results.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Taking into account the latest results, Nufarm's eight analysts currently expect revenues in 2027 to be AU$3.19b, approximately in line with the last 12 months. Nufarm is also expected to turn profitable, with statutory earnings of AU$0.08 per share. Yet prior to the latest earnings, the analysts had been anticipated revenues of AU$3.38b and earnings per share (EPS) of AU$0.13 in 2027. From this we can that sentiment has definitely become more bearish after the latest results, leading to lower revenue forecasts and a large cut to earnings per share estimates.

See our latest analysis for Nufarm

The analysts made no major changes to their price target of AU$3.61, suggesting the downgrades are not expected to have a long-term impact on Nufarm's valuation. Fixating on a single price target can be unwise though, since the consensus target is effectively the average of analyst price targets. As a result, some investors like to look at the range of estimates to see if there are any diverging opinions on the company's valuation. The most optimistic Nufarm analyst has a price target of AU$4.14 per share, while the most pessimistic values it at AU$3.25. This is a very narrow spread of estimates, implying either that Nufarm is an easy company to value, or - more likely - the analysts are relying heavily on some key assumptions.

Looking at the bigger picture now, one of the ways we can make sense of these forecasts is to see how they measure up against both past performance and industry growth estimates. We would also point out that the forecast 0.6% annualised revenue decline to the end of 2027 is better than the historical trend, which saw revenues shrink 1.8% annually over the past five years By contrast, our data suggests that other companies (with analyst coverage) in a similar industry are forecast to see their revenue grow 6.4% per year. So while a broad number of companies are forecast to grow, unfortunately Nufarm is expected to see its revenue affected worse than other companies in the industry.

The Bottom Line

The biggest concern is that the analysts reduced their earnings per share estimates, suggesting business headwinds could lay ahead for Nufarm. On the negative side, they also downgraded their revenue estimates, and forecasts imply they will perform worse than the wider industry. There was no real change to the consensus price target, suggesting that the intrinsic value of the business has not undergone any major changes with the latest estimates.

Keeping that in mind, we still think that the longer term trajectory of the business is much more important for investors to consider. We have forecasts for Nufarm going out to 2029, and you can see them free on our platform here.

You can also view our analysis of Nufarm's balance sheet, and whether we think Nufarm is carrying too much debt, for free on our platform here.
